title: ASL after the first lessons
description: Understand familiar signs from different people, work through similar movements and practice on short scenes.

blocks.text: After a beginner course in American Sign Language a person can sign a familiar thought themselves but needs more varied practice at understanding. The idea is a continuation with different signers, not a repeat of the same vocabulary in new packaging.

quote.text: I don’t think I’m fluent in ASL by any means, but more often than not I find that I can sign most if not everything I’m saying in English. I’m actually kind of sad that I finished it all!

blocks.text: Understand familiar signs from different people

A short scene is signed by different people. You can slow the video down, compare similar signs and go back to the detail that tells them apart. The topics are chosen for real communication: with relatives, colleagues or a visitor.

The material should be made and checked with ASL native signers and teachers. One course can’t be assumed to fit every sign language. It helps to test a few scenes after the beginner course first; promising fluent communication on finishing the set would be premature.
